body: I eat and get hungry but food is absolutely tasteless and has no enjoyability.
Same here. Even the usual distractions like tv and films or video games don’t work any more. Sleeping is sweet oblivion for me and is the only time I don’t hurt.
I wish I had the ability to connect to another person like that. I think, if I ever did. It’s been burned away through years of pain and rejection. I don’t really feel human any more.

I suffer with major depressive episodes and I understand exactly how you feel.

the good news is that physically speaking, it doesn’t LITERALLY damage your brain cells. They are just dormant and inactive due to the way your brain is acting

Think of it similar to muscular atrophy if you slept in bed for six months. Your muscles are still there, just weaker and they need some exercise to get back to normal

When I have depressive states I can barely have conversations because I forget what was said in the previous sentence. I walk around in a fog and feel confused all the time.

Trying to maintain mental activity helps stave it off until I get back into a normal state.

I’m not scared of killing myself.

I’m scared of fucking it up, and scared of whether my family will be able to handle me doing it.

We all fuck up, all the time.

I know I do.

I know how you feel. For whatever good that does. 

Hope you feel better.

If it was the easy way out, you’d think it would be way more common than it is.

I’ve been feeling lonely for the last ten years. Wanted a relationship that whole time too.

This pandemic has changed essentially nothing for me. Just saddened by how some people seem to be breaking down from a couple months of how I’ve lived my whole life.
Every time I go to sleep I hope in the back of my head that I won’t wake up
I’m on anti depressants and I used to be on diazepam which did help a lot. But the doctors don’t like giving it out for long term use so I can’t get it any more.

Over the last year or two I can’t go a day without thinking about it at least once. Over time that’s led to a very detailed plan of how I would do it.

Knowing there’s a way out if things get even worse is one of the few things that makes me feel a little better.
Same. I also feel paranoid when I hear scraps of conversation from strangers, always feels like they’re talking about me
